subject: Kellogg on-prem deployment: tenancy slices, PV strategy, and IO constraints
messages:
From: Alan Briggs <alan.briggs@kellogg.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0500
Subject: Kellogg on-prem deployment: initial constraints and site details

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the call today. I wanted to capture the high-level constraints from our infrastructure team before we lock in sizing: 

- Two sites: Warehouse A (primary) and Warehouse B (DR, read-only workloads).
- No internet egress for model artifacts from the primary site; artifact sync must be pull-pushed from a staging jumpbox under our control.
- Storage: each site has 2 x 1U NVMe shelves (local), and an NFS-backed SAN serving over a private VLAN for long term storage.
- Network: 10Gb internal fabric, but constrained cross-site WAN to 150 Mbps.
- Security: air-gapped-ish environment — outbound only to a specific proxy host.

We attached the site inventory export for the nodes we will make available (kellogg-site-inventory.csv). Our next milestone is a runbook review and a list of preflight checks.

Questions:
1) Do you need full images or is an init script sufficient for the jumpbox sync pattern?
2) Recommendations on node profiles for separating model-serving GPUs and workload orchestration?
3) Best practice for persistent volumes in this mixed local+SAN topology?

Alan
IT Architect, Kellogg Co.
Attachments: kellogg-site-inventory.csv
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alan Briggs <alan.briggs@kellogg.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kellogg on-prem deployment: initial constraints and site details

Alan,

Appreciate the inventory and constraints — that helps a lot. High level answers first, then a short proposal attached: proposed-node-profiles.pdf.

- Init script vs full images: init scripts are acceptable for the jumpbox approach but we recommend a validated golden image for GPU hosts to reduce driver/kernel mismatch risks. The jumpbox can handle model artifact staging and signature verification.

- Node profiles: our typical split is 
  * control/infra (small CPU nodes, reserved for kube-system and logging/metrics)
  * general compute (8-16 vCPU, 64-128Gi RAM) for non-GPU Redwood components and sidecars
  * GPU serving (one profile per GPU model, e.g., rtx-a6000 or ampere based) with local NVMe attached as ephemeral cache for KV caches and local shards
  * storage gateway nodes (higher network throughput, mounted to SAN) for long-lived PVs and backups

- Persistent volumes strategy: use local NVMe for hot KV and ephemeral caches (emptyDir backed by local device or local persistent volume) and NFS/SAN for long-term model artifacts and logs. We include a PVC binding policy and recommended reclaim/retention in the attached doc.

A few asks so we can finalize the runbook:
- Confirm whether the GPU hosts allow kubelet write access to local NVMe LVM or if only block device passthrough is permitted.
- Provide any procurement or maintenance blackout windows for site A.
- Confirm whether the DR site accepts asynchronous replication only (preferred) or synchronous replication for model artifacts.

Next step: once Dev and Marcus validate node profiles below, can we schedule a 60-minute runbook walkthrough? I put a tentative slot on Friday.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-node-profiles.pdf
From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Alan Briggs <alan.briggs@kellogg.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kellogg on-prem deployment: initial constraints and site details

Alan / team,

Following up with concrete sizing and PV recommendations. See attached k8s-pv-recommendations.md for a compact reference. Key points summarized here: 

1) Node counts (starting point for pilot, 3-node control plane + compute pools):
   - Control plane: 3 x m6-standard equivalent (2 vCPU, 8Gi) dedicated and isolated.
   - Infra (logging/observability/storage gateway): 3 x 8 vCPU, 32Gi RAM; these will host NFS clients and backups to SAN.
   - Compute (non-GPU): 4 x 16 vCPU, 128Gi RAM (workload orchestration + small model serving).
   - GPU serving pool: Start with 4 x A100-equivalent hosts, each with 4 GPUs (adjust after initial perf tests). Attach local NVMe for token KV cache and model shard ephemeral storage.

2) Storage classes and PV mapping:
   - sc-local-ephemeral (local PV, volumeMode: Block) for KV caches and mmapped shards. Use Local PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity + PodTopologySpread to keep requests near GPUs.
   - sc-san-standard (NFS backed RWX) for model artifacts, checkpoints, and logs; set reclaimPolicy: Retain and backup schedule nightly to DR.
   - sc-slow-object (object-store gateway) for cold model storage and archived artifacts.

3) IO & QoS considerations:
   - Limit eviction thresholds: ensure kube-reserved and eviction thresholds are tuned for bursty token generation.
   - Use cgroups/blkio limits on non-GPU tenants to prevent noisy neighbor on NVMe.

4) Airgap sync pattern:
   - Recommended: signed artifacts pulled to an air-gapped staging VM, scanned, then pushed into local registry. Provide a script and SHA256 checksums; golden images for GPU hosts should be validated via runbook step 3.

5) Security & auditing:
   - KMS integration for model key metadata is optional but recommended for audit trails.

Open questions from our side that would affect sizing/cost: expected concurrent request qps for serving and retention period for model checkpoints.

Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: k8s-pv-recommendations.md
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Alan Briggs <alan.briggs@kellogg.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kellogg on-prem deployment: tenancy slices, PV strategy, and IO constraints

Alan and team,

A couple of operational guardrails I want to add before we lock the runbook: 

- Local NVMe usage: treat NVMe as a cache layer only. Do not store single source of truth; copy critical checkpoints to SAN. We'll use LVM on top of NVMe for simpler snapshot workflows if the site allows kernel moduleload. If not, keep to raw block device with our sidecar manager.

- PVC binding & topology: include a BindingPolicy that restricts sc-local-ephemeral PVs to GPU nodes and sets a capacityReservation field to prevent overcommit. Example PVC sample saved as pvc-binding-policy.yaml.

- IO isolation: configure IO throttling at pod level for non-serving workloads, set burstable QoS for real-time serving pods. Provide PROMetheus metrics for nvme latency alerts (p99) and automated routing of degraded traffic to the DR model variant.

- Upgrade window: propose a rolling driver upgrade process using canary hosts to validate drivers before mass rollout. Add a maintenance blackout on the manufacturing calendar (please confirm blackout windows).

Happy to land these as discrete runbook checklist items. I can demo the PV binding policy during the walkthrough.

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pvc-binding-policy.yaml
From: Alan Briggs <alan.briggs@kellogg.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kellogg on-prem deployment: tenancy slices, PV strategy, and IO constraints

Jasmine / team,

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers:
- GPU hosts allow LVM and raw block access; we will provide a short checklist of kernel modules that have been preapproved.
- DR will be async replication; synchronous is out given WAN constraints.
- Blackout window: manufacturing freeze 2027-05-15 to 2027-05-22.

We approve the proposed pilot node counts for initial validation. Please send the final runbook and a calendar invite for the Friday walkthrough (ET slot preferred). I will loop in our AcmeOps vendor for assistance on physical install at Warehouse A.

Alan
IT Architect, Kellogg Co.
